title: The Fourier transform of the density is the partial Fourier transform of the kernel
source_title: Uniform semiclassical nonlinear Hartree phase mixing and weighted scattering for small perturbations

standard_prerequisites.name: Density of an operator
standard_prerequisites.statement: For an operator Q identified with its integral kernel Q(x,y), the density is rho_Q(x) := Q(x,x).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the object whose partial Fourier transforms are computed in the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Weighted Sobolev space H^0_{M,M}
standard_prerequisites.statement: H^0_{M,M} is the space of kernels whose weighted L2 norms up to order M are finite, with M = ceil((d+1)/2).
standard_prerequisites.use: The second half of the proof extends the identity from Schwartz kernels to this space by density.

standard_prerequisites.name: Sobolev embedding via Cauchy-Schwarz
standard_prerequisites.statement: Since M > d/2, the sup over k of the integral in p of the weight is bounded by the weighted L2 norms of the kernel up to order M.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the estimate at source lines 515-525 that gives absolute convergence uniformly in k.

core_obligations: Treat first the case of a Schwartz kernel: use Fourier inversion and Fubini to write rho_Q(x) as (2 pi)^{-2d} times the double integral of e^{i(k'+p) x} Qhat(k',p), and substitute k' = k - p (source lines 508-513).
Read off the first representation as the inverse Fourier transform of the bracketed function and obtain the second by the change of variables p -> k/2 - p (source line 513).

For general Q in H^0_{M,M}, set F_Q(k,p) := Qhat(k/2+p, k/2-p) and bound the sup over k of the integral in p of |F_Q| by the weighted Sobolev norms of Q, using Cauchy-Schwarz, the Sobolev embedding, and the two relations in which position and momentum multiplication become derivatives and multiplication by hbar p (source lines 515-525).

Conclude that both integrals converge absolutely and uniformly in k, and that the identity extends from Schwartz kernels by density, using Qhat(rho_Q)(k) = W[Q](k,0) together with the retained lemma on the Fourier representation of the Wigner transform (source line 527).

proof_roadmap.step: Schwartz case by Fourier inversion, Fubini and a substitution.
Uniform absolute convergence by Cauchy-Schwarz, Sobolev embedding and the position-momentum relations.
Extend to the weighted Sobolev space by density.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `densityofoperator` at source lines 500-506: for a kernel Q in H^0_{M,M} with M = ceil((d+1)/2), the Fourier transform of the density rho_Q(x) = Q(x,x) equals the partial Fourier transform of the kernel, in the two equivalent forms displayed. The proof (source lines 507-528) has to do two things that are independent: first the identity for Schwartz kernels, by Fourier inversion, Fubini and the substitution k' = k - p (lines 508-513), and then the extension to the weighted Sobolev space, which is not automatic because both sides must be shown to be continuous functionals, handled by a Cauchy-Schwarz and Sobolev-embedding estimate for sup_k of the p-integral (lines 515-525) in which the position and momentum multiplications are traded against the weight. Only after that does the density argument apply, and it is the retained earlier lemma that identifies the left-hand side with the Wigner transform at eta = 0 (line 527).
